subjects.displayTitle: Obedience and divine authority: love, recognition, and responsibility
subjects.introduction: Observe My commandments for the love of My beauty: the command, as Bahá’u’lláh frames it, is addressed to a lover rather than a subject, and that changes what obedience means. The Manifestation of God holds a sovereignty that no poverty, imprisonment or absence of followers can diminish, and once a soul has recognised Him, whatever He ordains carries the authority of a wisdom larger than the mind that receives it. Yet the same voice forbids coercion, insists that guidance reaches hearts only through kindness, and leaves conscience free to grow. Obedience therefore shows itself not in profession but in trustworthiness, generous sharing, steadiness in a storm, and conduct that brings tranquillity to others. Jesus’ words in John, that those who love him keep his word, offer a kindred way of seeing trust as inward before it is outward [1]. The journey continues into the Manifestation as the educator of humanity, the twin duties of recognition and obedience that His station calls forth, and the spirit that must animate obedience within administration.
subjects.arc: Begin with love, voluntary response, and freedom of conscience; examine recognition and the distinctive authority claimed for the Manifestations; trace obedience into character and community life; and close with service, wisdom, and tranquility.

order.why: Open with the command to obey for love of beauty and its demanding claim of authority.
shortened: The Tongue of My power hath, from the heaven of My omnipotent glory, addressed to My creation these words: "Observe My commandments, for the love of My beauty." Happy is the lover that hath inhaled the divine fragrance of his Best-Beloved from these words, laden with the perfume of a grace which no tongue can describe.

Whenever My laws appear like the sun in the heaven of Mine utterance, they must be faithfully obeyed by all, though My decree be such as to cause the heaven of every religion to be cleft asunder. He doeth what He pleaseth. He chooseth, and none may question His choice.

order.why: Immediately consider the Bab’s insistence on guidance through love without coercion.
Read attraction, generosity, and kindness as the way to reach hearts.
shortened: Strive, therefore, to create love in the hearts in order that they may become glowing and radiant. When that love is shining, it will permeate other hearts even as this electric light illumines its surroundings. When the love of God is established, everything else will be realized. This is the true foundation of all economics. Reflect upon it. Endeavor to become the cause of the attraction of souls rather than to enforce minds. Manifest true economics to the people. Show what love is, what kindness is, what true severance is and generosity.

order.why: Consider voluntary sharing as a practical expression of willing response.
Measure profession through deeds and firmness in a storm.
Read the reported test of correspondence between actions and principles.
shortened: A Baha'i must correlate his actions, words and affairs with the basic principles of the Blessed Perfection. If he sees that the former agrees with the latter, he may feel quite sure that he is on the right track. All our difficulties arise from the fact that our deeds do not correspond with the good pleasure of Baha'u'llah. With the presence of such a condition, it is passing strange that we still hope for benefic results.

order.why: Explore recognition, changing ordinances, and wisdom through the source’s extended argument.
shortened: The lesser intellect being thus circumscribed, one must search after Him Who is the ultimate Source of knowledge and strive to recognize Him. And should one come to acknowledge that Source round Whom every mind doth revolve, then whatsoever He should ordain is the expression of the dictates of a consummate wisdom. His very Being, even as the sun, is distinct from all else beside Him. The whole duty of man is to recognize Him; once this hath been achieved, then whatsoever He may please to ordain is binding and in full accordance with the requirements of divine wisdom.
Once the validity of a divinely appointed Prophet hath been established, to none is given the right to ask why or wherefore. Rather is it incumbent upon all to accept and obey whatsoever He saith.

order.why: Keep recognition of the claimed proof prior to the stated obligation to obey.
shortened: When it is established that he is the Throne of Truth, and thou witnesseth in his presence a proof that all creation is powerless to produce, then his word is God's Word, his command God's Command, his prohibition God's Prohibition, obedience to him is obedience to God, his good-pleasure is God's Good-Pleasure.

order.why: Read testimony, obedience, and unity of the Prophets together.
shortened: And should he encounter One Who layeth claim to a Cause from God, and Who holdeth from His Lord a testimony beyond the power of men to produce, he must needs follow Him in all that He pleaseth to proclaim, command and ordain, even were He to decree the sea to be land, or to pronounce earth to be heaven, or that the former lieth above the latter or below it, or to ordain any change or transformation, for He, verily, is aware of the celestial mysteries, the unseen subtleties, and the ordinances of God.

Know then that, inasmuch as all the Prophets are but one and the same soul, spirit, name, and attribute, thou must likewise see them all as bearing the name Muhammad and as being the son of Hasan, as having appeared from the Jabulqa of God's power and from the Jabulsa of His mercy.

order.why: Consider the reported analogies while retaining their prerequisite of recognizing true competence.
Read sovereignty that persists through poverty, abasement, and lack of followers.
shortened: Verily He Who is the Daystar of Truth and Revealer of the Supreme Being holdeth, for all time, undisputed sovereignty over all that is in heaven and on earth, though no man be found on earth to obey Him.

Though bereft of all earthly possessions, yet they soar in the realms of immeasurable riches. And whilst sore tried in the grip of the enemy, they are seated on the right hand of power and celestial dominion. Amidst the darkness of their abasement there shineth upon them the light of unfading glory, and upon their helplessness are showered the tokens of an invincible sovereignty.

order.why: Keep outward poverty beside the Prophets’ described station.
Read the reported distinction of the true teacher and trainer.
shortened: Similarly, these holy, divine Manifestations are and must always be distinguished above all other beings in every attribute of glory and perfection in order that it may be proven that the Manifestation is the true Teacher and real Trainer; that He is the Sun of Truth, endowed with a supreme splendor and reflecting the beauty of God.

order.why: Consider the prayer’s insistence that comparisons cannot contain the Manifestation.
Read the prayer concerning creation, names, and peerlessness in its own terms.
shortened: Wishing to reveal Thyself, Thou didst call into being the Greater and the Lesser Worlds, and didst choose Man above all Thy creatures, and didst make Him a sign of both of these worlds, O Thou Who art our Lord, the Most Compassionate!

Thou didst raise Him up to occupy Thy throne before all the people of Thy creation. Thou didst enable Him to unravel Thy mysteries, and to shine with the lights of Thine inspiration and Thy Revelation, and to manifest Thy names and Thine attributes.

I testify, moreover, that Thou hast decreed that none on the face of the earth should equal Them, and none of Thy creatures be able to be compared with any of Them, in order that Thine own singleness and peerlessness might be recognized and established.

order.why: Read knowledge and wisdom through the imagery of surging waters.
shortened: He is the Most Mighty Sign amongst men and the Dayspring of the most august attributes in the realm of creation.
Through Him the ocean of knowledge hath surged amidst mankind and the river of divine wisdom hath gushed out at the behest of God, the Lord of Days.

order.why: Consider the Manifestations as sources of wisdom for followers of all religions.
Hear the greeting to the guide of all nations.
Read the Seven Valleys’ praise of Muhammad through its names and images.
shortened: 2 And I praise and glorify that primal Sea which hath branched out from the ocean of the unseen Essence, and that primal Morn which hath broken forth upon the horizon of Singleness, and that primal Sun which hath risen in the heaven of everlasting splendour, and that primal Fire which was kindled from the Lamp of eternity within the Niche of oneness: He Who is called "Ahmad" in the kingdom of the exalted ones, and "Muhammad" amongst the concourse of the favoured ones, and "Mahmud" in the realm of the sincere; and in the hearts of the knowing, "whichsoever ye call upon, most beauteous are His names."

order.why: Consider the reported question about believing in successive Manifestations.
Read the relation between recognition, concealment, and overwhelming glory.
shortened: Were the Eternal Essence to manifest all that is latent within Him, were He to shine in the plentitude of His glory, none would be found to question His power or repudiate His truth. Nay, all created things would be so dazzled and thunderstruck by the evidences of His light as to be reduced to utter nothingness. How, then, can the godly be differentiated under such circumstances from the froward?

order.why: Keep the brief declaration of invincible sovereignty.
Face the strong claim that divine will exceeds prevailing human standards.
Read the explanation of the Most Great Infallibility within its stated scope.
shortened: In sum, the meaning of "He doeth whatsoever He willeth" is that if the Manifestation of God issues a command, enforces a law, or performs an action whose wisdom His followers cannot grasp, they should not think for a moment of questioning His words or actions. All souls are under the shadow of the universal Manifestation, must submit to the authority of the religion of God, and are not to deviate so much as a hairsbreadth.

order.why: Consider the physician image as the source’s account of superior diagnosis.
Read the claim concerning return and resurrection without weakening its challenge.
Keep the declaration of freedom to decree within its source setting.
shortened: Were He to decree for the heaven the decree of the earth, none has the right to object to Him, and were He to dispose of what is on earth, none has the right to say "why" or "wherefore." Everything hath proclaimed that He is the One Who ruleth as He pleaseth.

order.why: Read the concise prohibition of questioning the decree as stated.
Consider the obligation to follow within the source’s understanding of attainment.
Read the universal scope claimed for obedience.
shortened: Whoso obeyeth Him is saved and whoso turneth away is lost. It is incumbent and obligatory upon all the peoples of the earth, from its east and its west, its lands and its seas, its plains and its mountains, to obey Him in whatsoever is His good-pleasure.

order.why: Keep the declaration of creation for following.
shortened: Say: He is the One Whom the world must obey. He hath created all things for His following. This is what hath been decreed in the Tablet, were ye of those who know.

order.why: Read speech and the Pen as dependent upon divine leave.
Consider the stated dependence of deeds on leave and love.
shortened: The deed of no one is accepted save by His leave, nor doth the cry of any soul ascend except through His love. Thus hath the matter been decreed in the Tablets of God, the Supreme, the Mighty, the Beauteous.

order.why: Read turning toward the Manifestation as turning toward Truth.
Keep the severe contrast concerning rejection in its own scriptural wording.
shortened: Whoso holdeth fast unto Him hath surely held fast unto the cord of My loving-kindness and clung to the hem of My generosity. And whoso turneth away, he is of them that have attributed partners unto God's verses from time immemorial, and for him there is no portion of this mighty ocean.

order.why: Read the prayer describing the chosen messenger’s commission.
shortened: And when Thou didst purpose to unveil Thy sovereignty, and to glorify Thy word, and to reveal Thy bounteousness and mercy, Thou didst raise up one of Thy servants, and didst choose Him above all Thy creatures, and didst single Him out for Thy purpose, and didst clothe Him with the robe of Thy guidance, and didst immerse Him beneath the seas of Thy majesty and grandeur, and didst sanctify Him from all that beseemeth not the greatness of Thy glory and the power of Thy might, and didst bid Him to cry out before all that are in heaven and on earth, and summon the multitudes to the Manifestation of Thy Self and the Revealer of Thy signs.

order.why: Consider the testimony of speaking and breathing only by divine leave.
shortened: Thou knowest full well that I have not spoken a word but by Thy leave, that my lips have never been opened except at Thy bidding and in accordance with Thy pleasure, that every breath I have breathed hath been animated with Thy praise and Thy remembrance, that I have summoned all men to naught else except that whereunto Thy chosen ones have through all eternity been summoned, and that I have bidden them observe only the things that would draw them nearer unto the Day-Spring of Thy loving-kindness, and the Dawning-Place of Thy favors, and the Horizon of Thy riches, and the Manifestation of Thine inspiration and Thy revelation.

order.why: Hear worship of God joined with the Youth’s stated obedience.
shortened: This is a Book from this Youth to all who are on earth: Worship none but God, the King, the Most High, the Most Great.
He desireth naught except what your Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, hath desired for Him.

order.why: Read the reported description of the Manifestation as an example of obedience.
shortened: The Manifestation of God is a perfect example of real obedience. Like Him, we must sacrifice everything; every plan, every longing and ideal must be given up completely to the Will of God.

order.why: Keep the reported marriage decision as a personal account of response to a command.
Read the Bab’s concise instruction to receive and refrain.
shortened: O believers, whatsoever fruit of the Messenger He giveth you, accept it, and whatsoever He forbiddeth you, forgo it, for God hath made him wise in truth before Us.

order.why: Keep the address to Wahid and the preserved seal statement.
Read the Book of Permission in its addressed setting.
shortened: Read thou the Book of Permission unto him and say: The Command is from God. Fear thou God, for verily I see thee among the righteous ones.

order.why: Consider the reported divine command through the named speaker in the source.
shortened: And We have commanded the one who readeth this letter unto you both with commandments in the religion of God. When He commandeth you with a command, know that He speaketh naught except by My command.

order.why: Keep the selected statement of revealed verses and attained presence.
Read the warning to understand the station according to the Book.
shortened: Say: Regard Him not save as ye have been bidden in the Book. Fear God and be not of the ignorant ones.

order.why: Keep the warning against opposition in its revealed setting.
shortened: Say: O people, fear God and oppose not him who reciteth unto you the verses of God. Fear ye God, then fear His Cause, therefore fear Me.

order.why: Read the admonition concerning the bearer of the announcement.
shortened: Beware lest ye dispute with him after he has come to you from the Dayspring of Revelation with a momentous announcement that was inscribed in the Tablet.

order.why: Keep the companion warning concerning the bearer of verses.
shortened: Say: O people, oppose not him who hath come to you with the verses of God, your Lord and the Lord of the mighty throne.

order.why: Read sacrifice and the summons to follow the Tablets together.
shortened: O people! This is the Youth of God who standeth among you and calleth you unto the path of His good-pleasure. He hath sacrificed His soul for His Cause, the Mighty, the Powerful. Follow ye what hath been revealed in the Tablets and be not of them that turn aside. Cast not the Messenger of God behind your backs and be not of the lost.

order.why: Hear the appeal from the Wronged One to listen.
Consider hearing, acting, and contentment in one brief counsel.
shortened: Hearken unto the call of the Friend, act according to His bidding, and be content.

order.why: Read the priority of divine good pleasure over other approval.
Relates obedience to God to obedience to His Manifestation.
Trace knowledge of God into fear of God and steadfastness.
shortened: In sum: the spirit of the heart is the knowledge of God; its adornment is the confession that He doeth whatsoever He willeth, and ordaineth whatsoever He pleaseth; its robe is the fear of God; and its perfection is steadfastness.

order.why: Consider the source’s account of knowledge completed through action.
shortened: After arriving at this most exalted station, two things are necessary and obligatory for every soul: first, steadfastness in the Cause of God such that if all people should try to prevent him from the Source of the Cause they would be powerless to do so; and second, following the divine ordinances which have flowed from the fountain of the Pen of God's Will, for the knowledge of God is not complete and perfect except through following what He has commanded and what has been revealed in God's Book.

order.why: Read observance as the second necessary duty in its source context.
Keep steadfastness and action together as the two great matters.
Face the stated link between love and obedience.
shortened: I swear by God! Whoso faileth to obey the commandments of God can in no wise be numbered among His loved ones, for among the conditions of His love is to follow His commandments and observe His prohibitions.

order.why: Return to the direct command to act for love of beauty.
Hear the reported sweetness and firmness of obedience.
shortened: The sweetest thing in this world is to obey strictly the commands of God and shun His prohibitions. Through this the attractions of the Love of God will be created in human consciousness. If all the people of the world arise with swords in hands to detain him from carrying out the commands of God they will be unable to do so.

order.why: Consider humility and self-effacement within the language of sweetness.
shortened: His honor Sina commands thus, and I too desire to be obedient to the commands of the servants of the Blessed Beauty. And how sweet is this obedience! How much sweetness lies in this humility, submissiveness and self-effacement!

order.why: Read the Ayyam-i-Ha prayer’s image of chosen resolve.
Hear the prayer to listen before speaking and to act as bidden.
shortened: O Lord! Illumine their faces with the lights of confirmation and enlighten their hearts with the signs of unity, and make them aflame with the fire of Thy love in the realm of detachment, and make them among those of whom Thou didst reveal in the wise Remembrance, saying - and Thy word is truth - "They speak not before He hath spoken, and they do according to His bidding."

order.why: Consider the companion counsel to hear before acting.
shortened: Let us not speak before hearing, and not act before being commanded, so that we may be counted among those servants of whom He says: "They speak not before He speaks, and they act by His command."

order.why: Read spiritual insight alongside freedom from the dictates of desire.
shortened: Those who have been given spiritual insight from God are they who follow not the dictates of their desires, but hold fast unto that which they are commanded, and cleave to the cord of God and His Cause, and drink at all times from the cup of submission.

order.why: Keep the source’s contrast between following desire and receiving a command.
shortened: Among the people are those who cling to their vain desires, turning away from God, the Lord of all beings, and among them are those who cast away what they possessed and took what was commanded unto them from God, the Master of existence.

order.why: Read the warning against attributing passion-driven speech to God.
shortened: Methinks they have regarded the Divine commands as of no account, and considered the Lordly precepts as mere fancies. They speak as passion moveth them, then attribute what they say unto the One True God. He, verily, is clear of those who have wrought mischief in the land after it had been set in order, and who speak that which hath been forbidden them in the Book of God, the Lord of the worlds.

order.why: Join observance with rejection of corruption, dissension, and strife.
Consider trustworthiness made visible in human conduct.
shortened: We have manifested trustworthiness upon the temple of man, and verily he crieth out amidst the people of existence, saying: "All bounty belongeth unto him who hath clung unto me and acted according to that which was commanded by God, the Lord of all men."

order.why: Read the invitation for divine deeds to leave their fragrance in human action.
shortened: O people! Shun ye what ye have been forbidden in the Tablets, then walk in My footsteps that the fragrances of My deeds may waft from you among My creatures.

order.why: Join excellence toward others with acting on the Book.
Read the claim that divine commands intend the good of servants.
shortened: All have been created to hearken unto the Word of God and to follow His Cause. That which the Truth hath commanded and commandeth is and shall be for the good of His servants.

order.why: Consider order and tranquility among nations as stated purposes.
shortened: Today all who are on earth are obligated to follow the divine commandments, for these are the cause of order in the world and tranquility among the nations.

order.why: Read preservation of nations alongside a demand for wise conduct.
shortened: God willing, thou wilt in all conditions hold fast to the divine commandments which have been sent down in the revealed Books from the Supreme Pen, for this is the cause of the life of the world and the preservation of nations. God hath forgiven thee and thy father as a bounty from His presence. Verily, He is the All-Forgiving, the All-Bountiful. Today ye must conduct yourselves with the utmost wisdom and act in accordance with that whereby the Cause will be exalted.

order.why: Keep the hope for peace and security through following guidance.
Consider collective conduct as an invitation to others.
shortened: If they move according to the divine will and act upon that which hath been sent down in the Book, ere long will the world and its peoples turn towards the Dayspring of Revelation and quaff the choice sealed wine.

order.why: Read the reported counsel concerning responding to initial guidance.
Consider the companion reported statement about compliance and happiness.
Read the reported challenge of living a life of obedience.
shortened: To be killed for the Cause is not so difficult as to live for it in absolute obedience to the commands of God.

order.why: Keep the reported family counsel concerning obedience and sacrifice.
Read the reported statement about spiritual laws without making a medical claim.
Keep the account of the Black Stone as a reported explanation of obedience.
Read the reported volume of correspondence as context for personal guidance.
shortened: And my correspondence was so heavy that, at the time of the death of an American maidservant of God, my letters to her were counted and numbered sixty-seven; so you can imagine the situation!

order.why: Consider correspondence as a means of encounter despite separation.
shortened: Though the door of presence and speech be closed, yet through God's bounty the path of letters and messages remains open. "Correspondence is half of meeting" is evident and manifest.

order.why: Keep the letter’s account of correspondence and its source omission.
Read the instruction to study Tablets and act precisely.
shortened: Read the blessed Tablets and act precisely according to the teachings of the Blessed Beauty, letter by letter.

order.why: Hear appreciation for following counsel and advice.
shortened: Praise God that thou hast acted in accordance with the counsels of the Blessed Beauty and hast followed His instruction and advice.

order.why: Read the blessing on grasping ordinances and acting.
shortened: Blessed art thou for having held fast unto the cord of His ordinances and acted according to that which God hath revealed in the Book.

order.why: Consider hearing the Dove followed by response.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath heard what the Dove hath warbled and acted according to what his Lord, the Compassionate, the Forgiving, the Merciful, hath desired.

order.why: Read action valued above worldly possessions.
shortened: Act according to that which the All-Merciful hath revealed - this is better than all upon which the sun doth shine, if ye be of them who cleave fast to the commandments of their Lord, the Mighty, the Bountiful.

order.why: Keep the stated benefit extending through worlds.
Join attention to commands with contentment and gratitude.
shortened: Today all must fix their gaze upon the divine commandments and be content and grateful with utmost joy and delight in whatever He has ordained.

order.why: Read action beside the cord of lovingkindness.
shortened: Blessed is the state of the one who acted upon the divine counsels.
Hold fast to the cord of My loving-kindness and cling to the hem of thy resplendent Lord.

order.why: Consider assurance through grace and release from pride.
Keep grace and action together.
shortened: Hold fast to the hem of thy Lord's grace, then act according to what We have sent down in the Book.

order.why: Hear the counsel to act in a way worthy of the day.
shortened: Hearken unto the voice of the true Counsellor and act in accordance with that which is worthy of the Day of God.

order.why: Read recognition joined with observing limits.
shortened: Whoso hath recognized God will not transgress what God hath revealed in the Scrolls and Tablets.

order.why: Consider recognition becoming a station of action.
shortened: Praise be to God, they have attained to the recognition of Truth, of which most of the world remains deprived, and act according to His command. By My life, this is a mighty station with thy Lord, the Exalted, the Great.

order.why: Keep the description of nearness expressed through deeds.
shortened: They who have drawn nigh and acted according to what they were bidden - these are of the people of Baha in the Scriptures and Tablets.

order.why: Read attainment through following the revealed Cause.
Hear the concise statement of obligation.
Read action beside continued orientation to the horizon.
Keep the command concerning the revealed Book.
shortened: God hath decreed that every soul should act according to what hath been sent down in this Book which hath been adorned with the name of God, the Cleaver of the Dawn.

order.why: Consider submission with contentment in the source’s exact terms.
shortened: It is binding and obligatory upon every soul to obey the command of God. All must act according to that which hath been revealed in the divine Book and submit to it with perfect contentment. No one hath the right to transgress that which hath been commanded in the Book.

order.why: Read the contrast between observing and casting away the Book.
shortened: We have revealed the Cause and commanded all to observe what hath been sent down in the Book. Among the people are those who have acted in accordance with it and those who have cast it behind their backs - these are truly among the heedless ones in the Book of God, the Mighty, the Wondrous.

order.why: Keep the brief direction of attention toward divine commands.
shortened: However, all must fix their gaze upon the divine commandments and act in accordance with that which they have been bidden.

order.why: Join listening with refusal to follow mischief-makers.
shortened: O ye who are the beloved of the All-Merciful throughout all possibilities! Hearken unto that which God commandeth you in the Book, and follow not the way of the mischief-makers.

order.why: Read the particular limits on approaching and speaking.
Hear the prayer’s acknowledgment of commands past and future.
shortened: Say: I testify, O my God, in this my station, that Thou art the One Who is praised in what Thou hast done and wilt do, and art obeyed in what Thou didst command aforetime and wilt command hereafter.

order.why: Keep the concise appeal to act according to knowledge.
shortened: Act ye according to that which ye have been commanded by the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Read the source’s contrast of commanded action and desire.
shortened: Blessed is he who acts according to what is commanded, and woe unto him who casts behind him God's command and follows his own desires.

order.why: Hear the direct counsel to act.
Keep the statement concerning what is acceptable.
shortened: That which is acceptable in the sight of God this day hath been and shall ever be obedience to God, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Read refraining and acting as complementary responses.
shortened: Shun ye that which ye have been forbidden, then act according to that which ye have been commanded in the glorious Tablet.

order.why: Consider explicit attention to the Most Holy Book.
shortened: Today all must fix their gaze upon the divine ordinances and act in accordance with whatsoever hath been revealed in the Most Holy Book.

order.why: Keep the brief confirmation of the command’s source.
Hear the blessing upon attainment of commanded action.
shortened: Today the friends of God must act in accordance with that which hath been sent down from the heaven of His everlasting Command. Blessed is he who hath attained unto that which he hath been commanded in the Mighty Book.

order.why: Consider releasing what one possesses to receive what is offered.
Read attention toward revelation and its sufficiency.
shortened: Let them fix their gaze upon the horizon of the Cause and upon what is revealed from His presence, for verily He sufficeth all, and He is the Commander, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Keep the concise warning against transgressing the Book.
shortened: Beware lest ye transgress that whereunto ye have been bidden in the Book of God, the Mighty, the Most Praised.

order.why: Keep the paired warning and invitation concerning laws.
shortened: Fear ye God and commit not that which hath been forbidden you in every wondrous verse. Take ye the laws of God and that which He hath ordained in His Book, and be not of them that forsake them.

order.why: Read the brief statement pointing back to the Tablets.
shortened: O My loved ones! Prefer the love of God to the love of your own selves, and obedience to disobedience. This is what ye have been commanded in the Tablets, would ye but understand.

order.why: Hear the blessing on hearing and acting.
shortened: The glory be upon thee and upon those who have hearkened unto the call of God and acted according to that which they were commanded.

order.why: Keep the contrast between transgression and the paradise of wisdom.
Read the warning not to cast ordinances aside.
shortened: Say: Cast not the ordinances of God behind your backs, and be not of the heedless. Act ye according to what hath been sent down in the Tablets from the presence of One Who is knowing, informed.

order.why: Hear the brief direction attributed to the All-Merciful.
Keep the concise command concerning the Book.
shortened: Be thou steadfast in the Cause in such wise that the allusions of them that are on earth shall not withhold thee. Then act according to that which thou hast been commanded in His Mighty Book.

order.why: Read following the Book as the stated path.
Consider holding principles through bestowed strength.
Read the Book’s stated purpose of guiding action.
Keep the counsel and its contrasting responses.
Hear the blessing extended to those who act.
Consider the command described as bounty.
Join holding the Book with action.
Keep the concise blessing concerning obedience and remembrance.
Read fasting as a specific example of commanded practice.
shortened: These are the days wherein God hath prescribed the Fast unto His creatures. He, verily, is the One Who commandeth, the All-Knowing. They who circle round the Throne, and they who believed in Him when He was established upon His mighty throne, have observed the Fast. Blessed are they who follow the commandments of God - they, verily, are in an exalted station. Those who follow their own desires are numbered with the heedless.

order.why: Bring remembrance, praise, and action into prayer.
shortened: I call upon Thee, O Thou in Whose grasp are the reins of all religions, to assist me to remember Thee and praise Thee and to act in accordance with that which Thou hast revealed in Thy Book.

order.why: Hear the request to speak the Name and act according to the Book.
Consider a prayer encompassing Scriptures, Books, Psalms, and Tablets.
shortened: I beseech Thee to make me one of those who have circled round Thy will and acted in accordance with what they were bidden in the Scriptures, Books, Psalms and Tablets.

order.why: Join spiritual obedience with service to parents.
shortened: O God, I call on Thee with a tongue that hath spoken no word of disobedience against Thee, imploring Thee, by Thy sovereignty and might, to keep me safe in the shelter of Thy mercy and to grant me strength to serve Thee and to serve my father and mother.

order.why: Close with conduct that brings tranquility to other hearts.
Keep the individual responsibility to explore truth and the freedom of conscience in view.
Examine conscience as capable of growth and also of inherited prejudice.
shortened: ...conscience is never to be coerced, whether by other individuals or institutions. Conscience, however, is not an unchangeable absolute.

Conscience, therefore, can serve either as a bulwark of an upright character or can represent an accumulation of prejudices learned from one's forebears or absorbed from a limited social code. subjects.displayTitle: The House of Justice: consultation, care, and continuity
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh pictures a room in every city where counsellors sit as though they had entered the presence of God, charged to regard the interests of others exactly as they regard their own. That image sets the terms for everything the House of Justice is meant to be: not a seat of power but a trust, whose first duties are to take counsel, to protect human honour, to see that no child goes without schooling and no one is reduced to begging. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds that its members are freely elected, that they are guarded from error as a body though not as individuals, and that each day brings a new problem calling for a new answer, so laws made for one age may be unmade in another while the revealed Book stands. When the early church chose trusted people because its widows were neglected [1], it was learning the same lesson: care needs an institution to carry it. From here one can follow how elections shape such a body, how legislation differs from interpretation, what conferred infallibility claims, and how justice, upheld by reward and punishment, trains a world.

subjects.displayTitle: The purpose of religion: transformed lives and a more united world
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh puts a plain and searching question to every faith: has it changed anyone? The object of revelation, He teaches, is a transformation of the whole character of humankind, visible at once in the inner life and in the outward conditions of the world; where that change fails to appear, the coming of a Messenger has been for nothing. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sharpens the test with the figure of a remedy: religion exists to heal, and a cure that inflames the disease is no longer wanted. The purpose, stated again and again, is to protect the interests of the human race and bind it in unity, so that people come to see one another as leaves and fruit of a single tree and each believer pulses like a living artery in the body of mankind. Such a purpose asks for trustworthiness, kindness to the downcast, care for the rights of others, and a refusal to oppress. James’ demand that hearers become doers, tending widows and orphans, measures the same distance between profession and practice [1]. From here the path leads on to the Manifestation as divine educator, to love as the foundation of all religion, and to the unity of the religions themselves.
subjects.arc: Begin with inward and outward transformation and the test of healing; explore knowledge, education, character, and spiritual life; consider unity across human divisions; then return to everyday conduct, collective effort, and thoughtful service.

For if the character of mankind be not changed, the futility of God's universal Manifestation would be apparent.

order.why: Read the explicit purpose of safeguarding human interests and unity, with its qualification concerning false concord.
shortened: Such exhortations to union and concord as are inscribed in the Books of the Prophets by the Pen of the Most High bear reference unto specific matters; not a union that would lead to disunity or a concord which would create discord.

The Great Being saith:  O ye children of men!  The fundamental purpose animating the Faith of God and His Religion is to safeguard the interests and promote the unity of the human race, and to foster the spirit of love and fellowship amongst men.  Suffer it not to become a source of dissension and discord, of hate and enmity.  This is the straight Path, the fixed and immovable foundation.  Whatsoever is raised on this foundation, the changes and chances of the world can never impair its strength, nor will the revolution of countless centuries undermine its structure.

order.why: Make interdependence concrete through the tree and daily thoughtful help.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty saith: "Ye are all the fruits of one tree, the leaves of one branch." Thus hath He likened this world of being to a single tree, and all its peoples to the leaves thereof, and the blossoms and fruits. It is needful for the bough to blossom, and leaf and fruit to flourish, and upon the interconnection of all parts of the world-tree, dependeth the flourishing of leaf and blossom, and the sweetness of the fruit.

For this reason must all human beings powerfully sustain one another and seek for everlasting life; and for this reason must the lovers of God in this contingent world become the mercies and the blessings sent forth by that clement King of the seen and unseen realms. Let them purify their sight and behold all humankind as leaves and blossoms and fruits of the tree of being. Let them at all times concern themselves with doing a kindly thing for one of their fellows, offering to someone love, consideration, thoughtful help.

order.why: Invite the reader to become a living artery in the body of humankind.
Examine the twofold purpose of understanding and peace.
Connect righteousness and understanding with tranquility.
shortened: The purpose underlaying the revelation of every heavenly Book, nay, of every divinely-revealed verse, is to endue all men with righteousness and understanding, so that peace and tranquillity may be firmly established amongst them.

order.why: Read the virtues and good deeds named as the purpose of manifestation.
shortened: The purpose of the one true God in manifesting Himself is to summon all mankind to truthfulness and sincerity, to piety and trustworthiness, to resignation and submissiveness to the Will of God, to forbearance and kindliness, to uprightness and wisdom. His object is to array every man with the mantle of a saintly character, and to adorn him with the ornament of holy and goodly deeds.

order.why: Consider character, civilization, rights, and learning from other peoples together.
shortened: Universal benefits derive from the grace of the Divine religions, for they lead their true followers to sincerity of intent, to high purpose, to purity and spotless honor, to surpassing kindness and compassion, to the keeping of their covenants when they have covenanted, to concern for the rights of others, to liberality, to justice in every aspect of life, to humanity and philanthropy, to valor and to unflagging efforts in the service of mankind. It is religion, to sum up, which produces all human virtues, and it is these virtues which are the bright candles of civilization.

order.why: Place preservation of people and their rights beside trustworthiness.
shortened: Ever has God's purpose in sending Messengers, revealing Books, establishing firm laws and ordained religions been several things, among them the preservation of souls and their rights, and this depends on the appearance of the light of trustworthiness among people.

order.why: Join the prohibition on oppression with service for the betterment of the world.
shortened: It is not permissible to contend with anyone, nor is it acceptable in the sight of God to ill-treat or oppress any soul.
All men have been called into being for the betterment of the world. It behoveth every soul to arise and serve his brethren for the sake of God.

order.why: Read the refusal to cause sorrow across differences of faith.
shortened: Say: O people! Ye have stepped out of nothingness into the realm of being that ye may reconstruct the world. Dissension and strife ill beseem the station of a human being. In this day, should a soul become the cause of sorrow to another soul, no matter from which Faith, this would not be pleasing to this Wronged One. Unto this bear witness both Mine inner and outer tongue, and beyond them every wise and discerning, every learned and attentive soul. The fundamental purpose of religion as brought down from the heaven of divine Revelation is harmony and union among all people.

order.why: Bring grace into the concrete task of refreshing the downcast.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the Ocean of God’s mercy hath been manifested unto men, the Day in which the Daystar of His loving-kindness hath shed its radiance upon them, the Day in which the clouds of His bountiful favor have overshadowed the whole of mankind. Now is the time to cheer and refresh the downcast through the invigorating breeze of love and fellowship, and the living waters of friendliness and charity.

order.why: Hear the reported vision of religion as shelter and aid for the vulnerable.
shortened: They must keep the religion of God pure and uncontaminated, a haven of rest for the despondent souls, a safe harbor for the shipwrecked, a divine antidote for the ailing ones, a torch of light for those who are groping in the darkness, and a spiritual democracy for the down-trodden and the outcast.

order.why: Examine the remedy image alongside the destructive effects of prejudice.
shortened: His third teaching is that religion is a mighty stronghold, but that it must engender love, not malevolence and hate. Should it lead to malice, spite, and hate, it is of no value at all. For religion is a remedy, and if the remedy bring on disease, then put it aside. Again, as to religious, racial, national and political bias: all these prejudices strike at the very root of human life; one and all they beget bloodshed, and the ruination of the world. So long as these prejudices survive, there will be continuous and fearsome wars.

order.why: Keep the reported challenge to religious enmity in the Monnier conversation.
Read the Woking address’s question about wasting the Prophets’ labors.
Hear the Book of the Covenant’s purpose of extinguishing hatred.
shortened: The aim of this Wronged One in sustaining woes and tribulations, in revealing the Holy Verses and in demonstrating proofs hath been naught but to quench the flame of hate and enmity, that the horizon of the hearts of men may be illumined with the light of concord and attain real peace and tranquillity.
O ye that dwell on earth! The religion of God is for love and unity; make it not the cause of enmity or dissension.

order.why: Join justice, unity, fairness, and freedom from religious strife.
shortened: The word of God which the Supreme Pen hath recorded on the sixth leaf of the Most Exalted Paradise is the following: The light of men is Justice. Quench it not with the contrary winds of oppression and tyranny. The purpose of justice is the appearance of unity among men.

The word of God which the Supreme Pen hath recorded on the seventh leaf of the Most Exalted Paradise is this: O ye men of wisdom among nations! Shut your eyes to estrangement, then fix your gaze upon unity. Cleave tenaciously unto that which will lead to the well-being and tranquillity of all mankind. This span of earth is but one homeland and one habitation. It behoveth you to abandon vainglory which causeth alienation and to set your hearts on whatever will ensure harmony.

order.why: Read worldwide education and friendship across religions as a widened horizon.
shortened: We have erewhile declared - and Our Word is the truth -: 'Consort with the followers of all religions in a spirit of friendliness and fellowship.' Whatsoever hath led the children of men to shun one another, and hath caused dissensions and divisions amongst them, hath, through the revelation these words, been nullified and abolished. From the heaven of God's Will, and for the purpose of ennobling the world of being and of elevating the minds and souls of men, hath been sent down that which is the most effective instrument for the education of the whole human race.

order.why: Consider knowledge of God and fellowship while retaining the polemical passage’s historical target.
shortened: The Divine Messengers have been sent down, and their Books were revealed, for the purpose of promoting the knowledge of God, and of furthering unity and fellowship amongst men.

The utterance of God is a lamp, whose light is these words: Ye are the fruits of one tree, and the leaves of one branch. Deal ye one with another with the utmost love and harmony, with friendliness and fellowship. He Who is the Daystar of Truth beareth Me witness! So powerful is the light of unity that it can illuminate the whole earth.

order.why: Read friendly association and fairness as practices of regeneration.
Hear the summons to reconciliation and shared well-being.
shortened: This is the Day in which God’s most excellent favors have been poured out upon men, the Day in which His most mighty grace hath been infused into all created things. It is incumbent upon all the peoples of the world to reconcile their differences, and, with perfect unity and peace, abide beneath the shadow of the Tree of His care and loving-kindness. It behooveth them to cleave to whatsoever will, in this Day, be conducive to the exaltation of their stations, and to the promotion of their best interests.

order.why: Consider education and unity as the proper use of a precious life.
shortened: Deprive not yourselves, and waste not your precious lives in heeding the words of this one or that. Gird up the loins of endeavor and turn your attention to the education of the peoples of the world. Consider not the religion of God as a cause of opposition, rancor and hatred. The Tongue of Grandeur proclaims: That which hath been sent down from the heaven of the Will of God in this most holy and exalted Revelation hath been for the unity of the world and the love and fellowship of its peoples.

order.why: Read utterance as the stated instrument for removing rancor and conflict.
shortened: I declare by the Sun of Truth, which has shone forth from the highest horizon of the world, that the people of Baha had not and have not any aim save the prosperity and reformation of the world and the purifying of the nations. His intention is to cleanse the world through the waters of remembrance and utterance from rancor and hatred, that perchance religious strife and conflict, which are the cause and reason for the shedding of blood and the upheaval of the world of humanity, might be removed from its midst, so that all who dwell on earth might be adorned with the ornament of unity and concord and illumined with the light of love and harmony.

order.why: Join trustworthiness and reform with the hope of replacing military power through love.
shortened: This Wronged One beareth witness that servants have been brought from nothingness into being for the betterment, fellowship and unity of mankind. Corruption and conflict have ever been and are condemned. The divine Books, Tablets and Scriptures have given the glad-tidings that the purpose of this Most Great Manifestation is none other than the reformation of the world and its peoples, that perchance through the power of utterance military might may be abolished, and the world be governed through the power of love.

order.why: Keep the concise statement of removing conflict and hatred.
shortened: God is witness and aware that this Wronged One's purpose and desire is to remove strife, corruption and conflict from the world and to purify the hearts of all peoples from rancor and hatred.

order.why: Read the testimony concerning salvation and extinguished enmity.
shortened: The atoms of created things bear witness and the realities of all contingent beings testify that this servant had and has no purpose in the manifestation and proclamation of the Cause except the salvation of the servants and the extinguishing of the fire of hatred and enmity.

order.why: Consider hatred transformed into love through the fire-and-light image.
Hear the concise ambition to revive and ennoble the world.
Read betterment of the world as the purpose of creation.
shortened: All have been created for the betterment of the world.

order.why: Read the stated aim in the address to the Sultan.
Consider the common table offered to a quickened and united world.
Hear the prayerful testimony to life, unity, and salvation.
Read salvation, reform, harmony, and tranquility in one concise purpose.
shortened: For this Most Great Revelation has been dedicated to the salvation and reformation and unity and harmony and tranquility of the peoples of the world.

order.why: Consider guidance that preserves people and exalts their stations.
shortened: Their purpose hath been and still is the guidance of mankind. Whatsoever is the cause of preservation of the servants and the exaltation of their stations is recorded in the Books.

order.why: Read the goal of true liberty and spiritual freedom.
Face the Bab’s question of a life’s purpose beyond returning to clay.
Keep recognition and presence as the stated purpose of creation.
shortened: The purpose of all creation hath been and ever shall be the recognition of the Ancient Being and the assurance of attaining His presence.

order.why: Read the concise statement concerning recognition.
shortened: His purpose in this supreme mercy and mighty favor hath been and still is the recognition of Him by His servants.

order.why: Keep the contrast between creation’s purpose and rejection in its source setting.
Consider inward ennoblement as the essential purpose of faith.
shortened: The cornerstone of the Religion of God is the acquisition of the Divine perfections and the sharing in His manifold bestowals. The essential purpose of Faith and Belief is to ennoble the inner being of man with the outpourings of grace from on high. If this be not attained, it is indeed deprivation itself. It is the torment of infernal fire.

order.why: Read divine education as acquiring perfections and reflecting the image of God.
shortened: As to divine education, it is the education of the Kingdom and consists in acquiring divine perfections. This is indeed true education, for by its virtue man becomes the focal centre of divine blessings and the embodiment of the verse "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." This is the ultimate goal of the world of humanity.

order.why: Hear the reported question about the purpose of life and its answer concerning virtues.
Read the address’s questions about the prophetic mission as education.
shortened: Let me ask: What is the purpose of Prophethood? Why has God sent the Prophets? It is self-evident that the Prophets are the Educators of men and the Teachers of the human race. They come to bestow universal education upon humanity, to give humanity training, to uplift the human race from the abyss of despair and desolation and to enable man to attain the apogee of advancement and glory.

order.why: Consider the reported sequence of Prophets united through that educational purpose.
shortened: For what purpose did God send Moses? For what object did Christ appear? What was the mission of His Holiness Mohamad? Why did His Holiness the Bab step forth upon the arena of the world? For what cause did His Holiness Baha'u'llah manifest Himself? The answer is: The appearance of all these divine men is for no other reason save the education of the world of humanity.

order.why: Read successive religions through their stated work of education and illumination.
Consider latent powers and qualities awakened through education.
Read the mirror image as an account of the training of human realities.
shortened: The mission of the Prophets, the revelation of the Holy Books, the manifestation of the heavenly Teachers and the purpose of divine philosophy all center in the training of the human realities so that they may become clear and pure as mirrors and reflect the light and love of the Sun of Reality.

order.why: Join mental capacity, spiritual susceptibility, and a shared foundation.
shortened: To this end He has sent the Prophets of God, the holy Manifestations of the Word, in order that the fundamental reality and religion of God may prove to be the bond of human unity, for the divine religions revealed by these holy Messengers have one and the same foundation.

The purpose and mission of the holy, divine Messengers is the training and advancement of humanity, the cultivation of divine fruits in the gardens of human hearts, the reflection of heavenly effulgence in the mirrors of human souls, the quickening of mental capacity and the increase of spiritual susceptibilities.

order.why: Hear the reported sequence from ignorance and cruelty to wisdom and affection.
shortened: The aim of the prophet of God is to raise man to the degree of knowledge of his potentiality and to illumine him through the light of the kingdom, to transform ignorance into wisdom, injustice into justice, error into knowledge, cruelty into affection and incapability into progress. In short, to make all the attainments of existence resplendent in him.

order.why: Keep the demand for actual transformation of violent character into peace.
Read the fruit-bearing tree as the source’s image of cultivated potential.
Consider the cultivator and physician images without literalizing their imagery.
Join outward and inward perfections with knowledge and crafts.
shortened: Strive diligently to acquire both outward and inward perfections, for the fruit of the human tree has ever been outer and inner perfections. A person without knowledge and crafts is not beloved - like trees without fruit have they been and ever shall be. Therefore you must needs adorn, according to your capacity and means, the tree of your being with the fruits of knowledge and wisdom, of meanings and utterance.

order.why: Read the concern for lives constrained by trials and unrealized capacities.
shortened: As to those souls who are born into this life as ethereal and radiant entities and yet, on account of their handicaps and trials, are deprived of great and real advantages, and leave the world without having lived to the full -- certainly this is a cause for grieving. This is the reason why the universal Manifestations of God unveil Their countenances to man, and endure every calamity and sore affliction, and lay down Their lives as a ransom; it is to make these very people, the ready ones, the ones who have capacity, to become dawning points of light, and to bestow upon them the life that fadeth never.

order.why: Hear the reported need to care for spiritual as well as bodily life.
Consider the reported account of provision for spiritual needs.
shortened: Hence the proph[ets] have been set forth and the holy Scriptures revealed - so that they may provide an ample provision for the "spirit wants" of men, nurture them in the school of lofty idealism and enable them to extricate themselves from the capricious, binding laws of nature and give them the power to soar towards the realm of sanctity and spirituality.

order.why: Read the distinction between a polished mirror and the light it needs.
shortened: But the human spirit, unless it be assisted by the spirit of faith, cannot become acquainted with the divine mysteries and the heavenly realities. It is like a mirror which, although clear, bright, and polished, is still in need of light. Not until a sunbeam falls upon it can it discover the divine mysteries.

order.why: Keep the reported theological account of spiritual life and unity in its source terms.
shortened: The Prophets were sent to quicken this human spirit with the divine spirit. This is the spirit that causes the unity of the human world, the spirit that bestows eternal life, the spirit that confers everlasting felicity, the spirit that enables entry into the Kingdom of God, the spirit that transforms the earthly human into a divine being, the spirit that makes the terrestrial celestial, the spirit that changes darkness into light.

order.why: Read the address’s account of consciousness as a human faculty.
Consider knowledge, susceptibility, and spiritual powers as the stated glory of humanity.
shortened: The glory of man is in the knowledge of God, spiritual susceptibilities, attainment to transcendent powers and the bounties of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Keep the concise statement concerning spiritual distinction.
shortened: True distinction among mankind is through divine bestowals and receiving the intuitions of the Holy Spirit. If man does not become the recipient of the heavenly bestowals and spiritual bounties, he remains in the plane and kingdom of the animal.

order.why: Read attainable knowledge and attributes beside the limit of comprehending the divine Essence.
shortened: It is given to man to obtain knowledge, to attain to great spiritual perfection, to discover hidden truths and to manifest even the attributes of God; but still man cannot comprehend the Essence of God.

order.why: Consider the appeal for spiritual inquiry to advance with material investigation and to employ reason.
shortened: But according to the evidence of present world conditions divine philosophy -- which has for its object the sublimation of human nature, spiritual advancement, heavenly guidance for the development of the human race, attainment to the breaths of the Holy Spirit and knowledge of the verities of God -- has been outdistanced and neglected. Now is the time for us to make an effort and enable it to advance apace with the philosophy of material investigation so that awakening of the ideal virtues may progress equally with the unfoldment of the natural powers. In the same proportion that the body of man is developing, the spirit of man must be strengthened; and just as his outer perceptions have been quickened, his inner intellectual powers must be sensitized so that he need not rely wholly upon tradition and human precedent. In divine questions we must not depend entirely upon the heritage of tradition and former human experience; nay, rather, we must exercise reason, analyze and logically examine the facts presented so that confidence will be inspired and faith attained.

order.why: Keep the reported account of motion and progress in its historical philosophical setting.
Keep the reported workshop and crucible images, without presenting its metaphysics as established physics.
shortened: Yet man must ever remember the earth plane is a workshop, not an art gallery for the exhibits of powers. This is not the plane of perfection, but earth is the crucible for refining and moulding character.

order.why: Return to refinement of souls and divine unity as the stated purpose.
shortened: Otherwise those possessed of insight know with clear certainty that there has been and is no purpose save the refinement of souls and the manifestation of true divine unity.

order.why: Hear the reported definition of religion through human perfections.
shortened: Religion consists in the perfections of the world of humanity; it is the promotion of the perfections of the human world. These are obtained through the divine Teachings. The holy Manifestations of God appear for the sake of religion, that they may educate mankind in human perfections and promote the perfections of the world of man.

order.why: Connect the reported goal of moral progress with prosperity.
shortened: The object of all the religions has been the moral progress of the race;- then the illumination of the world will be assured and the prosperity of mankind obtained.

order.why: Read the stated relation between moral life and divine spirit.
shortened: The moral world is only attained through the effulgence of the Sun of Reality and the quickening life of the divine spirit. For this reason the holy Manifestations of God appear in the human world.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison with physicians and philosophers attributed to its speaker.
Consider the stated unity of religious purpose across differing traditions.
shortened: All the different religions of God that have risen on the face of the earth have one purpose: to educate man and to inform him of the spiritual, the luminous, the divine, so that he may partake of heavenly spirit and find eternal life, show forth the virtues of mankind, and from a world of darkness enter a world of light.
There is no other reality of meaning to the different religions. Their purpose is one, the teaching is one.

order.why: Read the expansive account of Christ’s purpose beyond founding a faction or securing acknowledgment.
shortened: The holy, divine Manifestations did not reveal themselves for the purpose of founding a nation, sect or faction. They did not appear in order that a certain number might acknowledge Their Prophethood. They did not declare Their heavenly mission and message in order to lay the foundation for a religious belief. Even Christ did not become manifest that we should merely believe in Him as the Christ, follow Him and adore His mention.

Nay, rather, Christ appeared in order to illumine the world of humanity, to render the earthly world celestial, to make the human kingdom a realm of angels, to unite the hearts, to enkindle the light of love in human souls, so that such souls might become independent, attaining complete unity and fellowship, turning to God, entering into the divine Kingdom, receiving the bounties and bestowals of God and partaking of the manna from heaven.

order.why: Keep the interpretation of Revelation within the commentary’s scriptural setting.
Read the common purpose of the Prophets through transformed worlds and organic unity.
Consider religion as the essential relationships of human unity.
Read separate streams becoming a sea and suffering undertaken for oneness.
shortened: What a blessing that will be -- when all shall come together, even as once separate torrents, rivers and streams, running brooks and single drops, when collected together in one place will form a mighty sea. And to such a degree will the inherent unity of all prevail, that the traditions, rules, customs and distinctions in the fanciful life of these populations will be effaced and vanish away like isolated drops, once the great sea of oneness doth leap and surge and roll.

And His reason for shouldering this heavy load and enduring all this anguish, which was even as an ocean that hurleth its waves to high heaven -- His reason for putting on the heavy iron chains and for becoming the very embodiment of utter resignation and meekness, was to lead every soul on earth to concord, to fellow-feeling, to oneness; to make known amongst all peoples the sign of the singleness of God, so that at last the primal oneness deposited at the heart of all created things would bear its destined fruit, and the splendour of 'No difference canst thou see in the creation of the God of Mercy,' would cast abroad its rays.

order.why: Keep the source’s analogies of union and separation in their own terms.
Read the reported material analogy for harmony without promoting it as scientific explanation.
Consider the images of clouds, flocks, and birds as an appeal to unity.
Read love and unity as conditions for fuller spiritual reflection.
shortened: That is to say, when this human body politic reaches a state of absolute unity, the effulgence of the eternal Sun will make its fullest light and heat manifest.
The more love is expressed among mankind and the stronger the power of unity, the greater will be this reflection and revelation, for the greatest bestowal of God is love.

order.why: Consider the invitation to a shared life beyond identities formed by desire.
shortened: How good it is if the friends be as close as sheaves of light, if they stand together side by side in a firm unbroken line. For now have the rays of reality from the Sun of the world of existence, united in adoration all the worshippers of this light; and these rays have, through infinite grace, gathered all peoples together within this wide-spreading shelter; therefore must all souls become as one soul, and all hearts as one heart. Let all be set free from the multiple identities that were born of passion and desire, and in the oneness of their love for God find a new way of life.

order.why: Read the image of distinct waves sharing one sea.
shortened: The dawning of the Morn of Guidance - the appearance of the Bab, may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him - and the rising of the Sun of Truth - the Ancient Beauty - and the endurance of all these hardships and tribulations were for the purpose that love and fellowship might be manifested in the human world, that hearts might be illumined and souls quickened by the breath of the All-Merciful, so that the friends of God who are attracted to the One Beloved might be as waves in form yet as the sea in essence - unity within unity.

order.why: Make oneness concrete in the address concerning racial fellowship in America.
shortened: When the racial elements of the American nation unite in actual fellowship and accord, the lights of the oneness of humanity will shine, the day of eternal glory and bliss will dawn, the spirit of God encompass, and the divine favors descend.

order.why: Read peace, freedom from prejudice, kindness, and gladness together.
shortened: The divine religions must be the cause of oneness among men, and the means of unity and love; they must promulgate universal peace, free man from every prejudice, bestow joy and gladness, exercise kindness to all men and do away with every difference and distinction.

order.why: Consider education, truthfulness, and bonds between East and West.
Read investigation as a duty directed toward the source of fellowship.
shortened: Therefore, it is our duty in this radiant century to investigate the essentials of divine religion, seek the realities underlying the oneness of the world of humanity and discover the source of fellowship and agreement which will unite mankind in the heavenly bond of love. This unity is the radiance of eternity, the divine spirituality, the effulgence of God and the bounty of the Kingdom.

order.why: Hear the reported purpose of investigating reality and religious unity.
Defines religion’s purpose as love and fellowship rather than contention.
Keep the reported account of enlightened minds and vanishing prejudice with its omissions.
Read the concise statement of prophetic love and agreement.
Consider suffering and sacrifice for the purpose of goodwill.
Hear the reported centrality of unity and goodwill.
shortened: The basis of the teaching of Baha'u'llah is the Unity of Mankind, and his greatest desire was that love and goodwill should live in the heart of men.

order.why: Read the shared purpose of peace through spiritual and material ordinances.
Consider religion described as a bond of morals and love.
Read the educational mission leading into peace and agreement.
shortened: The Prophets have appeared in this world with the mission that human souls may become the expressions of the Merciful, that they may be educated and developed, attain to love and amity and establish peace and agreement.

order.why: Keep unity rooted in human hearts.
Hear the reported account of light diffused across lands.
shortened: It was to manifest this light that Baha'u'llah was born, and came into the world. He taught Eternal Truth to men, and shed the rays of Divine Light in all lands.

order.why: Read the call for effort to make an envisioned unity real.
Keep the proclamation of oneness within the history of exile.
Read the costs of exile and hardship beside the stated purpose of unity.
Read the reported statement of love of God as a foundation.
Consider the scriptural connection of religion, moral restraint, and public welfare.
Keep the stated protection offered by ordinances in its revealed wording.
shortened: Indeed His ordinances constitute the mightiest stronghold for the protection of the world and the safeguarding of its peoples--a light upon those who acknowledge and recognize the truth, and a fire unto such as turn away and deny.

order.why: Read guidance and life through the light-and-darkness image.
shortened: If the light of religion did not exist, this world would be a realm of darkness, and if the spirit of life and guidance did not exist, humanity would be imprisoned in the grave.

order.why: Hear the reported summary of life, unity, honor, and progress.
Keep the categorical statement about political discussion in its source setting and with its omission.
Consider the reported counsel to associate for mutual illumination.
shortened: You must try to associate with those who will do you good and who will be the cause of your being more awakened, and not with those who will make you negligent of God.

Man must always associate with those from whom he can get light, or be with those to whom he can give light. He must either receive or give instructions. Otherwise, being with people without these two intentions, he is spending his time for nothing, and, by so doing, he is neither gaining nor causing others to gain.
You must keep these words very well.

order.why: Read receiving spiritual education as preparation to guide others.
shortened: A humble man without learning, but filled with the Holy Spirit, is more powerful than the most nobly-born profound scholar without that inspiration. He who is educated by the Divine Spirit can, in his time, lead others to receive the same Spirit.

order.why: Hear the companion account of reflected light becoming guidance.
shortened: God sent His Prophets into the world to teach and enlighten man, to explain to him the mystery of the Power of the Holy Spirit, to enable him to reflect the light, and so in his turn, to be the source of guidance to others.

order.why: Consider the reported call for every soul to become radiant.
Join words, actions, and a whole life in the image of illumination.
Read work with hands and feet beside inward spiritual attachment.
shortened: Your hands and feet will be working but your heart must be attached to the Almighty. The body of man is created for this world but his heart is made for the habitation of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Keep the brief invitation to endeavor and sacrifice.
shortened: Urge on the steed of high endeavour over the field of sacrifice, and carry away from this wide arena the prize of divine grace.

order.why: Close with the living artery as an invitation to quicken other hearts.
Connect inward and outward change with developing shared capacities.
Keep the difficult distinction between sincere belief and character.
Read the demand for living example that can bring hope.
Keep the separately supplied statement of betterment and tranquility.
Preserve the supplied statement attributed to Planck as an outside philosophical perspective.
Read Izutsu’s account of emanation and archetypes as its own philosophical analysis.
shortened: The creative movement, or, to use the technical terminology of wahdat al-wujud philosophy, the self-manifestation (tajalli) of the Absolute which is activated by the principle of love, emerges for the first time at the stage of ahadiyah and is called the 'most sacred Emanation' (Fayd-i-Aqdas). As the result of this Emanation, the stage of wahidiyah becomes established. The wahidiyah, is the ontological state at which the original absolute Oneness of the reality of existence appears with inner articulations.

The essential Perfections of God that are thus established in divine Consciousness with clear demarcations are called the 'eternal Archetypes' (a`yan thabitah). Structurally, each eternal Archetype is considered to be the zahir or exterior of [a] particular divine Name which is the batin or interior of the Archetype.
